rationale: M60.R8 (#749), the C7 framework trigger surface — the R8 census's ruby member. FOUR defects are pinned at once, and each one has a pre-fix observable this file would have produced: (1) DUPLICATION — the accumulator was a bare `metadata.detectedFrameworks!.push("Ruby on Rails")` called once per class and once per call, so this file published five identical entries; measured at five on a five-model file and three on rack/test.rb. (2) TWO NAMES FOR ONE FRAMEWORK — `detectedFrameworks` said "Ruby on Rails" while the pattern said "Rails", so the two published arrays could not be joined by name. (3) NO PRIMARY PICK — `metadata.framework`, the contract's deterministic pick, was published for nothing at all, so every file that DID detect Rails read as framework-less downstream. (4) AN UNREACHABLE TRIGGER — `before_action`/`after_action` are members of RAILS_MACRO_METHODS, whose branch RETURNS before the framework block, so the Callbacks pattern was unreachable in every execution: a file containing `before_action` published `frameworkPatterns: []` and this fixture is the only place that observable is holdable, since the metadata pins below compare the whole array. The pre-fix state fails all four pins at once; a mutant that reverts any single one of them fails the corresponding pin.

expectMetadata.comment: EXACTLY one entry. Pre-fix this was five.
the pattern carries the SAME name as the detection (it used to say "Rails"), and it exists at all only because the callback trigger is now reachable.

expectRelationships.comment: the association still emits its member and edge — the framework fix must not disturb the walk
